curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42096-1-1.pdf (one book; the functions are shown on pages 290-291)

functions.does: Pushed along, the rear wheels drive the flat six through a differential: half shafts with constant velocity joints run from the differential to the wheels, and the differential's ring gear turns a 20 tooth gear, which drives a 12 tooth gear on the crankshaft, so the six pistons run in and out of their cylinders in the two flat banks.
functions.source: book: steps 1-3 (differential), steps 108-110 (the engine fitted, page 65 on), page 291 (the engine's arrows)

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column runs forward through two universal joints to a 12 tooth gear, which turns a 20 tooth gear beside it; a pair of 16 tooth gears takes the turn down to a 12 tooth pinion on the steering rack between the front wheels.
functions.source: book: step 130 (the steering wheel), page 290 (the steering's arrows); the gear path to the rack is read from the model

functions.does: The two doors swing open on hinges at their front edges.
functions.source: book: page 290 (the arrows on the doors)

functions.does: The front wheels each have independent suspension: the hub rides between a lower and an upper suspension arm, and a shock absorber lets the wheel rise and fall.
functions.source: book: page 290; the front axle's arms and shock absorbers are built in the front axle steps
functions.note: the shock absorbers' springs only matter under force; worked by hand the wheel should rise and fall with its arms

functions.does: The rear wheels have independent suspension too, on pairs of arms with a shock absorber each.
functions.source: book: page 291 (the double arrow on the rear wheel); the rear arms and shock absorbers are built in the first steps, with the differential
functions.note: as for the front: the springs only matter under force
